Author: Anders Hartvoll Ruud <andruud@chromium.org>

Perform monospace-related adjustment using true parent style

There is currently some code in FontBuilder that tweaks the specified
font size if the current generic font family changes to or from
monospace. This code assumes that the FontDescription stored on the
ComputedStyle pre-CreateFont is the inherited FontDescription, but
this is no longer (always) true.

This means that declarations like font-size:1em can be applied (and
subjected to CreateFont) twice, which means that the second call to
CheckForGenericFamilyChange won't detect a change in the
monospace-ness, hence the specified size will fail to adjust.

This CL fixes this by propagating the actual parent style to
CheckForGenericFamilyChange.

Generated extension API schemas implicitly depend on other APIs

Extension APIs generate a number of files based on the extension schema inputs.  When the inputs change, the output files are updated.  Generally, this works.

There can also be interdependencies between APIs; that is, API <A> may depend on a concept from API <B>.  In this case, the generated files for API <A> #include the generated files from API <B>.  This, too, generally works.

There's an issue where some of the generated code in API <A> can implicitly pull details in from API <B>.  In particular, adding a new enum to API <B> can result in a parse error message in API <A> changing.  This is a problem because we don't know to regenerate API <A> when API <B> changes.  There's a few options to fix this:
1) Properly track all dependencies, and regenerate any affected APIs whenever an API changes.  That is, regenerate <A> when <B> changes.
2) Just regenerate all APIs whenever any API in the module changes (APIs between modules should declare their own gn dependencies, so that should "just work").
3) Don't have generated code in API <A> be affected by changes in API <B>.

While 1) sounds nice, it's also finicky and much harder to get right.  2) would slow down build time for developers (and our CQ).  3) should do the trick and, at least in this case, is relatively easy to implement.  Additionally, it's conceptually desirable -- an API file's contents should be generatable from its own schema; dependencies should be in #includes, but not in the content of the generated file.

This was the cause of a recent revert; I'll look into fixing it.

[Extensions] De-tangle generated file dependencies

There was an implicit dependency between generated API files where, if
API <A> depended on API <B> and had an enum from API <B>, the generated
file for API <A> would include the expected strings from API <B>. This
led to an issue because changing API <B> would result in a required
change in API <A>, but our build system wouldn't regenerate it --
resulting in a deterministic build failure.

Fix this by moving the error messages for enum parsing out from the
callsite and into a separate method on the API to which the enum
belongs. This way, API <A> doesn't change at all when API <B> does.

(I also explored having the parse method return a base::expected rather
than introducing a new method for returning a parse error, but that's
a much farther-reaching change.)

PDF Viewer: Perform Select All only in response to Ctrl+A

Currently, the PDF Viewer looks for "Ctrl" and "A' to determine if it
should perform a Select All command, where "Ctrl" is "Cmd" on macOS.
This will also incorrectly match other key combinations, like
Ctrl+Shift+A, which is the keyboard shortcut for Tab Search.

Fix this by adding a hasCtrlModifierOnly() utility function and using
that instead of the existing hasCtrlModifier() function. Audit other "A"
key handling in PDF Viewer code and consistently use
hasCtrlModifierOnly().
